title: Freelancing: 6 steps to attract clients and win repeat work
summary: A practical checklist for new freelancers on getting hired. It covers listing on platforms, tapping personal networks, narrowing your niche, staying responsive, earning repeat work, and bringing in collaborators honestly.

principles.text: Platform traffic helps, but how you sell yourself decides whether you get hired.
principles.quote: Although the website traffic matters in terms of you getting hired, in the end, it all boils down to how you “sell” yourself to employers.

principles.text: Don't rely on platforms alone; tell your personal circle, whose referrals carry built-in trust.
principles.quote: Connect with your social circles and make your services known to those whom you know personally.

principles.text: Sell a specific niche, not a vague skill label, because clients hire for specific jobs.
principles.quote: Instead of generalizing your skills, try to sell within your niche specifically.

principles.text: Be proactive: apply to gigs yourself and price a bit below peers, but not so low it signals poor work.
principles.quote: Make it reasonable, yet lower than most freelancers.

principles.text: Respond fast and update often to build client confidence and ensure on-time delivery.
principles.quote: Furthermore, remember to be as responsive as possible — answer whatever queries clients have as soon as you receive them and always be professional and polite.

principles.text: Exceed expectations, then pitch follow-on projects; impressed clients trust you with more work.
principles.quote: If they’re thoroughly impressed with your previous work, then the chances of them trusting you on the work that follows are high.
